guitar.modelsText: Gibson SG Special / Rickenbacker / Fender Stratocaster / Gibson J-200
guitar.evidence: Pete Townshend's Gibson SG Special (smashed on stage, used on Live at Leeds) and earlier Rickenbackers are extremely well documented; deserves high rather than medium confidence given how iconic his windmill/SG combo is.
guitar.notes: Upgraded confidence from medium to high.

tone.target: jangle-clean intro with chiming delay-free 12-string feel; dry crunch rhythm later
tone.profile: jangle-clean intro with chiming delay-free 12-string feel; dry crunch rhythm later
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain emphasizing a Vox AC30-style clean tone for the arpeggios, followed by a slightly dirtier British combo sound for the driving rhythm sections. Compression is used lightly to maintain clarity.
corrections: Drop chorus and clean delay wash
Lean into the iconic chiming guitar intro

rig.name: The Who - Baba O'Riley - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain clarity during arpeggios.
Slightly lift the high end and maintain brightness for the chiming tone.
Provide subtle grit and definition for the driving crunch rhythm without heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: Using Red Haze for controlled breakup, mimicking a light overdriven tube amp feel.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, chimey sound of a Vox AC30 for the intro arpeggios.
Provide a classic British clean platform that supports the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: While not strictly an AC30 cab, this provides the necessary vintage UK voicing.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper mids and treble to achieve the 'chiming' arpeggio brightness.
Add a subtle, rhythmic echo effect to enhance the arpeggiated feel without sounding like a wash.
blocks.gap: The goal is 'delay-free' but adding a controlled delay helps define the chiming quality. Settings are kept minimal.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle sense of space without sounding like heavy reverb.
blocks.gap: Keeping the mix low is crucial to avoid 'big reverb' as requested.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for both the chiming clean intro and the driving rhythm sections.

proposals.reason: The current UK Vintage 4x12 is too large and muddy for the delicate, chimey arpeggios.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in upper mids.

proposals.reason: A smaller, tighter cab will better support the controlled breakup and punchy rhythm tone.
proposals.expectedGain: Tighter low end response and improved definition under drive.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Vintage British Combo IR (e.g., AC30 style)
proposals.reason: Using a single, cohesive cab model will unify the clean and crunch sections.
proposals.expectedGain: More authentic and consistent vintage British voicing.
